pl-l4d31c1-d1e115.summary: Turns to the goods of marriage and how they excuse intercourse.

pl-l4d31c1-d1e118.summary: States that marriage has principally three goods.

pl-l4d31c1-d1e121.summary: Quotes Augustine: the nuptial good is threefold, faith, offspring, sacrament: in faith, that after the conjugal bond one not unite with another; in offspring, that it be lovingly received and religiously raised; in sacrament, that the marriage not be separated and the dismissed spouse not be joined to another, even for offspring.
claims: Faith, offspring, and sacrament are the goods of marriage.

pl-l4d31c1.summary: Turns to the goods of marriage and how they excuse intercourse. There are three principal goods, as Augustine says: faith, not uniting with another after the marriage bond; offspring, received lovingly and raised religiously; and sacrament, that the marriage not be separated and neither dismissed spouse marry another, even for offspring.
claims: Marriage has three goods: faith, offspring, and sacrament.
Faith excludes other unions; offspring means loving reception and religious upbringing; sacrament means indissolubility.
